data.title: Moody's Upgrades Hungary Outlook, Citing Improved EU Relations
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Moody's Ratings changed its outlook on Hungary's government to stable from negative.

Alongside that, it affirmed Hungary's Baa2 long-term issuer and senior unsecured ratings and its Baa2 foreign-currency senior unsecured shelf rating.

Moody's said the upgraded outlook reflects reforms and improvement in Hungary's relations with the European Union. That improved relationship has reduced governance-related risks.

Anti-corruption institutions in the country have also strengthened. Renewed access to E.U. resources, improved investor sentiment and a concrete fiscal consolidation program all support prospects of economic growth and lower debt.

The Baa2 ratings reflect a balance between Hungary's relatively high income levels and diversified economy with its elevated government debt and continuing policy constraints.

Moody's also upgraded the issuer rating of Hungary's national bank to stable from negative, affirming the Baa2 issuer rating. The bank's credit profile is closely intertwined with the government and is influenced by the same credit fundamentals, Moody's said.

Hungary's local and foreign currency ceilings remain unchanged at A1.

data.title: Moody's lifts Hungary outlook to stable on reforms, EU ties
data.description:
Credit ratings agency Moody's on Friday revised Hungary's outlook to "stable" from "negative," citing institutional reforms and improved relations with the European Union.

Since taking office in May, Prime Minister Peter Magyar has secured the release of €16.4 billion ($18.01 billion) of previously frozen European Union funding after pledging to roll back reforms introduced under former Prime Minister Viktor Orban that Brussels argued undermined democratic institutions.

The release of EU funds is expected to support growth in an economy that has struggled to regain momentum following three years of stagnation.

Investors have welcomed the government's efforts to repair relations with the European Union and put Hungary on a path towards adopting the euro within the next decade, supporting a rally in the forint and government bonds.

Moody's said institutional reforms implemented since the change of government, including strengthened anti-corruption bodies, accession to the European Public Prosecutor's Office and renewed access to EU funding, had significantly reduced governance-related risks.

It affirmed the country's 'Baa2' sovereign rating.

($1 = 0.9107 euros)

data.title: Tongda, Membership E-Commerce Platform, Files for NASDAQ IPO
data.description:
Tongda International Group Co., Ltd filed a preliminary F-1 registration statement for an initial public offering of 5,000,000 ordinary shares. The company estimates a price range of $5 to $6 per share and has applied to list on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol TDHG. Tongda operates a membership-based e-commerce platform through subsidiaries in China.

Business Description

Tongda operates a membership-based e-commerce platform through its subsidiaries in China. The platform offers everyday goods, fashion, beauty products, electronics, luxury items, and products promoted as exclusive to members. The company says it earns revenue through product sales, membership subscriptions, and platform services or commissions.

Market Overview

  • Total addressable market: The filing estimates China's e-commerce transaction volume at nearly RMB 20 trillion in 2024 and projects it to exceed RMB 30 trillion by 2027.
  • Market growth: The filing reports approximately 17.6% year-over-year growth in China's e-commerce market in 2024 and projects about 15% annual growth over the following three years.
  • Market position: Tongda describes itself as a membership-based e-commerce platform; the filing does not provide independent market-share data.
  • Key competitors: The filing identifies Alibaba's Taobao and Tmall, JD.com, and Pinduoduo as major Chinese e-commerce platforms, and Amazon Prime and Costco as membership-model examples.
  • Industry trends: The filing highlights personalized recommendations, social commerce, faster logistics, online-offline integration, and sustainability-focused products.

Operational Metrics

  • Members: The filing describes a community of more than 500,000 active members.
  • Community engagement: The company reports more than 10,000 monthly discussions.
  • Product inspections: The filing says a team of 50 experts conducts more than 1,000 product inspections monthly.
  • Geographic presence: Operations are conducted through subsidiaries in China; the company plans to enter five additional domestic markets and three international markets over three years.
  • Delivery: The company reports average delivery times of 2–3 business days for most products and a delivery success rate above 98%.
  • Planned member events: Tongda aims to hold at least 20 exclusive member events annually.

Financials Highlights

  • Revenue (current): HK$20.4 million for fiscal 2025, as stated in the filing.
  • Revenue growth: Approximately 465% from HK$3.6 million in fiscal 2024 to HK$20.4 million in fiscal 2025.
  • Net income: $514,300 for fiscal 2025 and $823,500 for fiscal 2026, as stated in the filing; the fiscal 2026 figure is inconsistent with the November 20, 2026 filing date.

IPO Structure

  • Issuer: Tongda International Group Co., Ltd
  • Filing date: November 20, 2026
  • Proposed ticker: TDHG
  • Exchange: NASDAQ
  • Price range: $5 to $6 per ordinary share
  • Offering size: 5,000,000 ordinary shares; approximately $25 million gross proceeds at the assumed $5 offering price
  • Shares offered: 5,000,000 ordinary shares
  • Use of proceeds: Approximately $3.75 million for product expansion, $12.5 million for expansion into Asian markets, and $8.75 million for platform technology upgrades; remaining proceeds for general corporate purposes.

Original SEC Filing: Tongda International Group Co., Ltd - F-1 - Nov. 20, 2026

data.title: Oracle says OpenAI infrastructure deal is fully funded after final capital raise
data.description:
Oracle said on Friday that its infrastructure contract with OpenAI is fully funded following a final capital raise earlier this month.

Shares of Oracle rose as much as 3.3% in after-hours trading.

  • The comments follow investor scrutiny over the amount of capital Oracle would need to fund its expansion of AI data centers and its growing exposure to OpenAI

  • Oracle and OpenAI plan to develop 4.5 gigawatts of additional data-center capacity in the US, on top of the initial Stargate site in Abilene, Texas

  • "The financing we outlined at Oracle Investor Day, including vendor financing, is in place. Any further private discussions with vendors are just additional options," Oracle said in a post on X

  • The company also said that its Abilene campus, where OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra was trained, is nearly complete

  • Its next gigawatt-scale campus in Shackelford County, Texas, is fully permitted, and the handover of Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin racks is on track for the coming weeks, Oracle said

  • Oracle announced a $20 billion capital raise earlier this month, consisting of about $10 billion in stock and $10 billion in debt

data.title: Allied Critical Metals Provides Clarification of Technical Disclosure, Announces Results of Annual Meeting and Provides General Corporate Updates
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 20, 2026) - Allied Critical Metals Inc. (OTCQB: ACMIF) (FSE: 0VJ0) ("Allied" or the "Company") is providing the results of its annual shareholder meeting and a general corporate update on certain of its prior disclosure.

Clarifying Technical Disclosure

As a result of a review by the British Columbia Securities Commission, the Company is clarifying certain scientific and technical disclosure regarding its Borralha Tungsten Project ("Borralha") and Vila Verde Tungsten Project ("Vila Verde") in northern Portugal.

The Company has identified restricted and potentially ambiguous disclosures in certain of its news releases, the third quarter 2026 corporate presentation (the "Presentation"), website and related investor relations materials under National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects ("NI 43-101"). The Company is retracting and clarifying the disclosure identified below, including statements concerning the preliminary economic assessment for Borralha (the "PEA"), the historical estimates at Vila Verde, production decisions and qualified person identification.

The PEA is preliminary in nature and includes Inferred Mineral Resources that are considered too speculative geologically to have the economic considerations applied to them that would enable them to be categorized as Mineral Reserves. There is no certainty that the PEA results will be realized. Mineral Resources are not Mineral Reserves and do not have demonstrated economic viability.

The following corrections relate to the Company's March 2, 2026 news release entitled "Allied Critical Metals Delivers Robust Initial PEA at the Borralha Project" (the "March Release"), the Presentation, website and related investor relations materials. Investors should not rely on the statements and presentations of information expressly retracted below. This news release presents the Borralha PEA base-case economic results alongside two lower-price and two higher-price sensitivities on a consistent basis. This news release does not restate the PEA's numerical economic results.

  • "Robust Economics". The Company retracts the characterization "Robust Initial PEA" in the March Release's headline, "Robust Economics" in its Key Highlights, and the statement in the CEO quotation that the initial PEA "confirms the Borralha Project as a high-return, capital-efficient tungsten development project", together with equivalent characterizations in subsequent news releases and related materials. These descriptions suggested a level of certainty inconsistent with the preliminary nature of a PEA and the cautionary disclosure required by sections 2.3(3)(a) and 3.4(e) of NI 43-101. Although the March Release included PEA cautionary language, these characterizations did not appropriately reflect those qualifications. The PEA assesses potential economic viability; it does not establish technical or economic viability. It includes inferred mineral resources that are too speculative geologically to have the economic considerations applied to them that would enable them to be categorized as mineral reserves, and there is no certainty that the PEA will be realized. Mineral resources that are not mineral reserves do not have demonstrated economic viability.
  • Higher-price scenarios and upside presentation. The March Release prominently presented a "Medium Case" and a "High Case", alongside an Argus long-term "Base Case". The Company acknowledges that the presentation of those scenarios should also have included corresponding downside sensitivity in order to provide a balanced assessment. Although Section 7.6 and Figure 1 of the March Release included a broader price sensitivity analysis, the prominent presentation of favourable scenarios was not balanced by equivalent downside disclosure alongside those scenarios. Accordingly, the Company retracts the prior unbalanced presentation and replaces it with the below restated sensitivity analysis for the Borralha Project, which presents investors with a balanced range of potential outcomes based on differing commodity price assumptions. Investors should consider all scenarios together, and no single scenario should be viewed in isolation.

The Borralha PEA mine plan was developed using a tungsten price assumption of approximately US$659/mtu WO₃. The economic Base Case applies Argus's year-by-year tungsten price forecast, which averages approximately US$704/mtu WO₃. The four sensitivity cases use the same mine plan, production schedule and other modelling assumptions, with each case applying its stated fixed tungsten price over the mine life.

The US$704/mtu WO₃ base case remains the principal case for the Borralha PEA. The table below presents the base case alongside two lower-price and two higher-price sensitivities. Each of the four sensitivity cases applies a constant tungsten price over the life of the mine using the Base Case mine plan, production schedule and other modelling assumptions. These are sensitivity cases and do not replace the base-case assumption or constitute forecasts of future prices.

The analysis varies the tungsten price while holding the mine plan, production schedule and other technical and economic assumptions constant. It therefore measures the effect of price changes on the existing PEA development case and does not represent a separately optimized mine plan for each price. The prices shown are benchmark prices. Realized tungsten revenue per mtu produced reflects concentrate payability and applicable commercial deductions, including treatment and refining charges. All-in sustaining cost (AISC) is expressed per mtu produced. As a result, the project can have a negative NPV even when the benchmark price exceeds the AISC per mtu produced. The after-tax NPV at an 8% discount rate also reflects the initial capital investment and the timing of project cash flows. At US$306/mtu and US$400/mtu WO₃, the modelled after-tax NPVs are negative US$234 million and negative US$134 million, respectively.

The lowest-price sensitivity is not presented as an economic break-even price. Economic outcomes are determined by the cash-flow model, including capital expenditure, operating costs, commercial deductions, royalties and taxation.

Canadian dollar equivalents for the two new lower-price sensitivities are approximate and use the same exchange rate as the previous disclosure, C$1.3658 per US$1.00. This range is provided for market context. The PEA base-case price assumption is approximately US$704 per mtu of WO₃ price forecast.

The PEA is preliminary and includes Inferred Mineral Resources. Their geological uncertainty precludes treating them as Mineral Reserves on the basis of this economic assessment. There is no certainty that the PEA will be realized. Mineral Resources that are not Mineral Reserves do not have demonstrated economic viability.

  • PEA results in the Presentation. The Company retracts that presentation of the PEA results in the Presentation, as the disclosure did not fully satisfy the conditions in section 2.3(3) of NI 43-101. Investors should not rely on the PEA results as presented in the Presentation. The economic results in Table 1 of this news release should be read together with the accompanying assumptions, qualifications and cautionary disclosure, including the preliminary nature of the PEA and its inclusion of Inferred Mineral Resources. The Company will ensure that future disclosure of a PEA that includes inferred mineral resources includes an explanation of the basis of the assessment and its qualifications and, with equal prominence, the caution that the assessment is preliminary in nature, includes inferred mineral resources that are too speculative geologically to have the economic considerations applied to them that would enable them to be categorized as mineral reserves, and that there is no certainty the assessment will be realized.
  • Vila Verde historical estimates. The Presentation presented historical estimate information for Vila Verde in a manner that could be interpreted as treating those estimates as current mineral resources. The Company retracts that characterization and any related disclosure in its website and investor relations materials that conveyed the same impression. A qualified person has not done sufficient work to classify the historical estimates as current mineral resources or mineral reserves, and the Company is not treating them as current mineral resources or mineral reserves. Investors should not rely on those historical estimates as current estimates. The Company will remove any presentation suggesting otherwise.
  • Production decision. The Presentation contained disclosure that could be interpreted as indicating that the Company had made a production decision. The Company retracts any implication in the Presentation that it has made a commercial production decision in respect of either Borralha or Vila Verde, including in respect of any pilot plant. The Company confirms that it has made no such decision for either project. The pilot plant testwork contemplated at Vila Verde is intended to inform further technical evaluation of that project. The Company has not completed a feasibility study supporting mineral reserves for either project, and the PEA does not establish the technical or economic viability of production or provide the same level of confidence as a feasibility study. The production schedules, mine-life estimates and processing assumptions disclosed in the March Release describe a conceptual PEA scenario, not a commitment to construct or achieve production on those schedules. The March Release identified further drilling, metallurgical testing, geotechnical and hydrogeological investigations, engineering toward a pre-feasibility study and further permitting as recommended work.
  • Qualified person identification. The Presentation did not identify the qualified person who prepared, supervised the preparation of, or approved its scientific and technical information or disclose that person's relationship to the Company, as required by section 3.1 of NI 43-101. The Company confirms that the preparation of the scientific and technical information that formed the basis for the scientific and technical disclosure contained in the Presentation derived from the Borralha PEA and the Vila Verde Technical Report were supervised by Vítor Arezes, MIMMM, QMR #703197, Vice President Exploration of Allied Critical Metals Inc., a Qualified Person as defined by NI 43-101. The Company will correct that omission in the Presentation and other applicable written technical disclosure. The qualified person references for this news release are set out below.

The Company acknowledges its responsibility for disclosure made by it or on its behalf and is committed to complying with NI 43-101 and applicable scientific and technical disclosure requirements. The Company has enhanced its internal disclosure review processes to support accurate, balanced, factual and non-misleading communications and to ensure that scientific and technical disclosure is based on information prepared by or under the supervision of, or approved by, an appropriately qualified person and includes the required disclosure of that person's identity and relationship to the Company.

The Company is undertaking an immediate review and correction of its website, corporate presentation, social media and other investor relations materials to address the issues identified above and remove other non-compliant or misleading technical information.

Qualified Persons

The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Vítor Arezes, MIMMM, QMR #703197, Vice President Exploration of Allied Critical Metals Inc., a Qualified Person as defined by NI 43-101.

Annual Meeting of Shareholders

The Company is pleased to announce that shareholders of the Company ("Shareholders") have approved all matters brought before the annual general and special meeting of Shareholders (the "Meeting") held on October 22, 2026, as outlined in the management information circular of the Company dated September 21, 2026 (the "Circular") prepared in connection with the Meeting.

The Blanket Order is a Canadian securities regulators' pilot program that allows eligible venture issuers to voluntarily move from quarterly to semi-annual financial reporting.

The Company's fiscal year ends on December 31. Under the SAR pilot program, the Company will be exempt from filing interim financial reports and related management's discussion and analysis ("MD&A") for its first and third quarters, subject to satisfying the applicable conditions of the Blanket Order. Accordingly, the Company will not file interim financial reports or related MD&A for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, or for subsequent first- and third-quarter reporting periods ending March 31 and September 30, respectively, while the Company remains eligible to rely on the exemptions under the Blanket Order.

The Company will continue to file audited annual financial statements and related MD&A (due within 120 days of December 31) and six-month interim financial reports and related MD&A (due within 60 days of June 30), together with the required certifications. The Company remains committed to timely disclosure and will continue to report all material changes and significant developments in accordance with National Instrument 51-102 Continuous Disclosure Obligations and applicable TSX Venture Exchange requirements.

The Company confirms that it meets the eligibility criteria under the Blanket Order. The Company has determined that participation in the SAR pilot program will ease the administrative and financial burden associated with quarterly reporting and is consistent with the objectives of the Blanket Order.

Right to participate in the extraordinary general meeting and notice of participation

Participation at the meeting venue

(ii) notify the Company of their participation no later than 16 December 2026 by post to Sleep Cycle AB (publ), "Extra bolagsstämma december 2026", Drakegatan 10, SE-412 50 Gothenburg, Sweden, or by e-mail to investor@sleepcycle.com. The notification shall include the shareholder's name, personal identification number or corporate registration number, address, telephone number and the number of any assistants (not more than two) as well as, where applicable, information about any proxy.

A shareholder represented by proxy shall issue a written and dated power of attorney for the proxy. Power of attorney forms are available on the Company's website, investors.sleepcycle.com. If the power of attorney is issued by a legal entity, a registration certificate or equivalent documents of authority shall be enclosed. To facilitate registration at the meeting, the power of attorney as well as the registration certificate or other documents of authority should be received by the Company at the above address no later than 16 December 2026.

Shareholders wishing to participate in the meeting by postal voting must (i) be entered in the share register kept by Euroclear Nordics AB relating to the circumstances on 14 December 2026, and (ii) notify the Company of their participation no later than 16 December 2026 by casting their postal vote in accordance with the instructions below, so that the postal vote is received by Sleep Cycle no later than that day. Nominee registered shares

data.title: Clean-Energy Investors Look Beyond Carbon Emissions — Market Talk
data.description: Private-market investors looking to capitalize on the economy's transition to clean energy favor strategies aimed at boosting the security and resilience of energy sources, rather than just reducing carbon emissions, according to Australian infrastructure specialist IFM Investors. "For investors, it is no longer enough for energy to be renewable; it must also be resilient," IFM says in a report. As an example, it cites Australia's power market, where abundant solar sources often lead to negative wholesale electricity prices. "Standalone solar is less compelling for institutional investors," IFM says. "Solar power paired with battery storage, however, is a different proposition." In Europe, too, investors' appetite for renewables varies with markets and technologies, IFM says. "We see growth in transmission, onshore wind and battery storage, but less attractive returns in offshore wind." (luis.garcia@wsj.com; @lhvgarcia)
